title.narrative: Weoog Paani "New forest" in Burkina Faso 2019-2024
Weoog Paani "Ny skog" i Burkina Faso 2019-2024

description.narrative:
Projektet Weoog Paani (”Ny skog”) i Burkina Faso syftar till att stödja tillämpningen i större skala (25 landsbygdskommuner) av den modell för lokal skogsförvaltning som den icke-statliga organisationen (NGO) Tree Aid utvecklat och testat i 8 landsbygdskommuner i Burkina Faso. Modellen innehåller främst följande steg:
- Kartläggning av resurser genom skogsinventering och markkartering - Socio-ekonomiska enkäter - Utarbetande av skogsbruksplaner med deltagande av intressenter (byföreningar, lokala småföretag, kommunrepresentanter etc) - Förnyelse av skog, stärkt biologisk mångfald och ökad skogstillväxt tillsammans med lokala organisationer, byorganisationer, statliga skogsrådgivare och skogsforskare - Anläggande av mikrovattenfördämningar i skogarna i avsikt att öka CO2-upptag, stärka biologisk mångfald och öka skogsprodutionen - Marknadsstudier för att identifiera värdekedjor (produkter) med ekonomisk potential och med relevans för sårbara hushåll - Stärkande av värdekedjor (produktion - förädling - marknadsföring) - Stöd till lokala småföretag och främjande av hållbara mikrofinanslösningar för dessa
Kvinnor och ungdomar ges ett särskilt fokus. Utbildning av såväl lokala grupper, småföretagare som representanter för kommun respektive stat är en viktig del av projektet. Statliga aktörer deltar dels genom miljöministeriets ordförandeskap i projektets styrkommitté, dels genom att statliga (främst skogliga) rådgivningsorgan agerar enligt sina mandat och normala roller.
Projektet genomförs av ett konsortium av tre organisationer: - Tree Aid - en internationell icke vinstdrivande NGO med säte i England och specialiserad på lokal skogsförvaltning. Tree Aid är ambassadens avtalspartner. - SNV - en internationell NGO med stor erfarenhet av privatsektorutveckling (inkl värdekedjor) inom jordbruk i Afrika - United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) - ett FN-organ med lång bakgrund inom mikrofinans i Burkina Faso Dessutom pågår ett nära samarbete med miljöministeriet i Ouagadougou samt skogsmyndighetens rådgivningsorganisation i fält.
Projektets aktivitetsperiod löper från 1 juni 2019 till 31 maj 2021. Sverige bidrar - såsom ensam givare - med 79 miljoner kr, varav 1 miljon kr hanteras direkt av ambassaden för revisioner, utvärdering och uppföljning. Ambassaden och Tree Aid avser att förlänga avtalet med ytterligare tre år, dvs till 31 maj 2024, med bibehållen årlig volym på budgeten.

The project Weoog Paani (“New forest”) in Burkina Faso aims at implementing at a large scale (25 rural communes/municipalities) the local forest management model that the non-governmental organization Tree Aid has developed and tested in 8 rural communes in Burkina Faso. The model contains the following main steps:
- Mapping of resources through forest inventories and land maps - Socio-economic surveys - Preparation of forest management plans together with local stakeholders (NGO, community organizations, local small enterprises, commune representatives etc) - Forest regeneration, strengthened biological diversity and improved forest production together with village organisations, forest extension services and forest researchers - Establishment of micro water dams in the forests in order to increase CO2 sequestration, increase biological diversity and increase forest production - Market studies to identify value chains with economic potential and relevance for vulnerable households - Strengthening of value chains (production - processing - marketing) - Support to local small enterprises och promotion of sustainable micro finance solutions
The Project particularly focuses on women and youth. Capacity building of local groups, small businesses and representatives of communes and government services is an important part of the Project. The government takes responsibility for the Project by the Ministry of Environment's chairmanship of the Project Steering Committee and by the role of its extension services at regional and local level.
The Project is implemented by a Consortium of three organizations: - Tree Aid - an international non-profit NGO with its head office in the United Kingdom and specialized on local forest governance - SNV - an international NGO with broad experience in Africa of private sector & value chain development in agriculture - The United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) - a UN organization with a long background within micro-finance in Burkina Faso
The Project's activity period will last from 1 June 2019 to 31 May 2021. Sweden is the sole donor and provides a budget of 79 million SEK, of which 1 million SEK will be handled by the Embassy i Ouagadougou for audits, follow-up and evaluation. The Embassy and Tree Aid intend to sign an agreement amendment extending the project with 3 years to 31 May 2024 with approximately the same annual budget amount.

The development objective is "Sustainable improvement of the living conditions of the rural population in the target zones through improved governance of forest resources, investments in the forests and the valorization of non-timber forest products while contributing to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals" ("Amélioration durable des conditions de vie des populations rurales de la zone dintervention du projet à travers la promotion de la gouvernance locale des ressources forestières, les investissements dans les forêts et la valorisation des PFNLs et ce dans loptique de la réalisation des Objectifs du Développement Durable").
The specific objectives refer to improved local forest governance, improved sylviculture and increased income for vulnerable households and are formulated as follows:
1. Promote an enabling environment for local governance of forest resources in 25 municipalities in 5 regions 2. Strengthen the regeneration, preservation and production capacities of forest areas 3. Increase the incomes of actors through the improved economic importance of forest resources

The project logframe includes 157 (!) indicators and in many cases targets set were achieved/surpassed. Below follows a list of selected results. Please note that this is just a selection not a complete list (available in the final report of the project). The number within parentheses is the target.
Specific Objective 1: Promote an environment conducive to local governance of forest resources, the most important activities and results in 2023-2024 were:
- The forest governance was improved in 11 communes bringing the number from 7 to 18 (18).
- Forest production was increased from 5 to 8% (10%).
- Revenue from non-timber forest products was increased by 18% (5%).
- The percentage of community members who were pleased with local forest governance increased from 25% to 69% (60%).
- Forest area with a management plan increased from 22827ha to 31863ha (28552ha). The number of forest management plans in the project area increased from 15 to 22 (20).
- The number of local bylaws increased from 15 to 34 (20).
Specific Objective 2: Strengthen the regeneration, production and preservation potential of forest areas and community adaptation to climate change, the most important activities and results in 2023 were:
- The area of degraded land that has been recovered increased from 15844ha to 32336ha (50500ha).
- The total number of trees through regeneration, planting, transplanting and direct seeding increased from 961366 (reference) to 5303856 (5806228) with a survival rate of 70% (which is very good).
Specific Objective 3: Increase stakeholders' income through the economic development of forest resources, the most important activities and results in 2023-2024 were :
- The total income from community forest enterprise increased from 217 445 196 FCFA to 1 209 712 744 FCFA (1 087 225 980 FCFA).
- The number of community forest enterprises based on non-timber forest products in the area increased from 318 to 462 (targeted increase was 150).
Again, this is just a selection of results produced.
Unexpected results in 2023-2024:
- The involvement of internally displaced persons in project activities has facilitated their integration into host communities.
- Establishing contacts at trade fairs forged relationships with exhibitors abroad. For example, the Coordination of grassroots organizations of Po and Fada benefited from trips to Abidjan, Bamako and Dakar to exhibit their products.
- The valorisation of residue from shea butter production into briquettes and charcoal has won prizes at innovation fairs, and business relations for these products are under construction.
Additional results
After the end of the project Treeaid produced a nice publication called "Localising forest governance in Burkina Faso: 2007-2024" documenting their results and lessons learnt from the Swedish-funded contribution and projects funded by other donors. The publication shows how Nature-based solutions (NbS) tackle climate/environment challenges and poverty in an integrated way. Treeaid continues to work on forest governance in Burkina Faso after the withdrawal of Sweden.
Just after the end of the Swedish funded project the Tond Tenga project became the first in the world to be registered using a new, globally approved standard for high-quality carbon credits. It is therefore now officially registered under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), using Verras methodology for afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (VM0047) that was recently approved by the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market (ICVCM). This in turn means that all the carbon credits the project generates will carry the Core Carbon Principles (CCP) label a mark of trust and quality in the carbon market. Treeaid has shown their ability to draw on new sources of funding for rehabilitating degraded land and generating income for vulnerable people.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
